type.description: the protocol that turns the address into files (protocols/): http, one file per address, an archive (by the end of its name: .zip, .tar, .tar.gz, .tgz, .tar.bz2, .tbz2, .tar.xz, .txz) unpacked into its members; git, a repository on any host at the commit its address serves, its large files through LFS (a Hugging Face dataset is one, at https://huggingface.co/datasets/<owner>/<name>); mercurial, a repository at its tip; empty: no upstream, the patches hold every file (text written for WPT)

address.description: where to fetch it; what upstream serves there when asked is what is taken. The source's id is given when it is created and never derived from the address again, so an address that changes keeps its source. With `addresses`, the first of them

addresses.description: http only: several addresses, each fetched (with the source's extract rules) into its own folder of the source's tree; `address` repeats the first one's address

folder.description: the folder at the tree's root that this address's files go into

strip.description: leading path components removed from every path

name.description: http only: the file's name, which says whether it is an archive, when the address's last path part does not give it; a file that is not an archive keeps it as its path

history.description: git only: the commit history from `since` to the commit the download gets, one file `.git/history/<commit>` per commit without merges, in git format-patch layout, limited to the files `extract` keeps

since.description: the first commit kept: the one from which the repository's root license file holds the license the source lists

submodules.description: git only: the address of each kept submodule, by its path from the source's root (a submodule's own submodules too); its files are read at the commit the tree pins. An excluded submodule needs none

license.description: SPDX identifier or LicenseRef-<name>, or an expression: alternatives joined by OR, licenses that apply together joined by AND, each optionally WITH an exception

paths.description: the files the entry covers: exact paths, or patterns that name a folder (`src/*`, `src/**`) or a kind of file, in every folder (`**/*.js`) or in the top folder (`*.js`); a pattern made only of wildcards (`**` alone) is refused. Every file is covered by exactly one entry; the records of a records file, each by the one entry whose field place expects its value

attribution.description: the credit this license asks for, written by a person: authors, title, copyright line, link

place.description: where the license statement must be found: a file of the content (the covered file itself too), a field of each record, a page at an outside address (downloaded with the source), or the entry itself

file.description: a path of the source's tree

field.description: a field of each record of the records files the entry covers; the entry covers the records whose field holds one of its expected values

entry.description: the signed entry's text is the statement, accepted as it stands; only where no statement can exist in the content: the text WPT writes itself, in an empty source, and a public-domain proof (LicenseRef-public-domain)

expected.description: what the statement at `place` must be: at a file or a page, the ids of the license texts (data/license-texts/<id>/) it may match; at a field, the values of a record's field the entry covers, exactly as the records hold them (other values as JSON). A record whose value no entry expects is covered by none. None for the entry itself

text.description: the license text as the source gives it (its LICENSE file, with its copyright line, and an Apache NOTICE file's content); for LicenseRef-public-domain, why the work is in the public domain. Every model trained on the source carries it in its NOTICE. Empty only while the source's decision is refused (a person writes it later); any other decision needs a text

decision.description: whether this entry's license is accepted, signed by a person; a file trains only when its source, its entry and the license text found at its place are all admitted. A save that changes the entry's license, place or expected texts without deciding it anew sends it back to under-review

formats.description: how each file becomes Markdown for training; every path matches exactly one entry

format.description: markdown: kept as is; text: plain text; xhtml: web pages as strict XML (EPUB books); html: web pages that are not strict XML (such as Project Gutenberg's), converted as xhtml pages are; code: a fenced code block naming the language and the path; chat: conversations for the training step the file's tags name, never a pre-training document; task: the files of task folders (task.json, files/, check) for the training step the tags of their task.json name, never a pre-training document; rating: people's pass or fail ratings of measure attempts, one per line, a measure only, never a pre-training document nor a training signal; records: a JSON Lines (.jsonl, .json, optionally .gz or .zst) or Parquet file holding one document per record, each with its own license, or a JSON document holding the list of records (`records`), or an XML file holding one record

language.description: code only: the language named after the opening fence, for example python

text.description: records only: the field holding the document's text (in an .xml file, every field is an XPath 1.0 expression)

as.description: records only: whether the text field is plain text (default), Markdown, or a web page converted as an html file is

records.description: records only: the file (.json, optionally .gz or .zst) is one JSON document, and this field of it holds the list of records

namespaces.description: records only: the prefixes the XPath fields of an .xml records file use, each mapped to its namespace

join.description: records only, for .xml files: each record also reads the one file of `paths` whose path holds the same key, as the XPath variable $<name> (an empty node set when no file holds it); those files give no document

name.description: the XPath variable holding the joined file's document

paths.description: the files that can be joined

key.description: a Python regular expression searched in the record file's path; its groups, joined by one space (its whole match when it has none), are the key

joined_key.description: the same, searched in each joined file's path

id.description: records only: the field holding the record's id within its file; without it, the record's position (1 for the first)

newest.description: records only: the field holding the record's date (ISO 8601); of the records that share an id in all the files this entry covers, only the one with the latest date is read, and when the dates are equal the later one (in path order, then in its file); without it, an id that repeats in a file is an error; it needs `id`

title.description: records only: the field holding the record's title, which becomes the document's first line as a heading

credit.description: records only: the fields that name the record's authors, title and address, copied into the per-record credit file of every model trained on it

keep.description: records only: a record enters only when each rule's field holds one of its values

in.description: the values kept, exactly as the record holds them (other values as JSON)

tree.description: chat only: the file holds one message per record (JSON Lines or Parquet, as a records file), each naming its parent; every path from a first message to a last one becomes a conversation (docs/chat-format.md)

parent.description: empty or absent for a first message

roles.description: the file's role names, each mapped to WPT's

drop.description: a message matching one rule is dropped, with everything after it

is.description: drop when the field holds exactly this value

above.description: drop when the field holds a number above this one

held_out_by.description: which documents are held out together: where `pattern` is found in a document's path, the held-out hash reads the pattern's groups joined by one space (its whole match when it has no group) instead of the document's id, so documents of any source with the same groups share their fate (docs/data-selection.md, "Held-out text and contamination")

pattern.description: a Python regular expression, searched in the document's path

cuts.description: erasure cuts (docs/erasure.md), applied in this order before the patches; made with `wpt-dataset cut`, which needs the store's cut key

path.description: the upstream file the passage is removed from

hmac.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the passage under the store's cut key

rolling.description: the passage's rolling hash under the store's cut key

decision.description: the source's decision: whether WPT wants the source at all (docs/data-selection.md), signed by a person

address.description: empty:<name>, a name for the source; nothing is fetched

reason.description: required to refuse; optional under review; to admit, only for an exception (such as an explicit permission for content without a license)

glob.description: path pattern: * matches within one folder, ** across folders

field.description: a record field; dots go into nested objects, for example metadata.license
